newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo predicts U.S. Zantac sales drop.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo predicts U.S. Zantac sales drop.

text.p: British pharmaceutical group Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Thursday that sales in the U.S. of its best-selling ulcer drug Zantac could drop by up to 80 percent in the 12 months after it loses its patent in July.

"If you take the worst-case scenario, between July 1997 and July 1998, it could be possible to lose 70 to 80 percent of Zantac sales in that marketplace," chief executive and deputy chairman Richard Sykes told a news conference.
Sykes said Zantac accounted for around 30 percent of Glaxo Wellcome's total U.S. sales of 3.683 billion stg last year.
The company said that sales of Zantac in Germany, which was the first major market to face generic competition, fell by 43 percent last year.
The company faces a further challenge with the loss of the U.S. patent on herpes drug Zovirax in April. Around one third of Zovirax's 812 million stg sales last year were in the U.S..
"There will be many generic competitors and that business will go very quickly," Sykes told reporters.
